title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement:
Return the maximum value in every contiguous window of a fixed size.

Contract
- `numbers` is non-null and non-empty; `windowSize` is between 1 and `numbers.length`.
- Return an array of length `numbers.length - windowSize + 1`, where result i is the maximum of the window starting at i.
- Do not mutate the input array.

Examples
- `maxSlidingWindow(new int[]{1, 3, -1, -3, 5, 3, 6, 7}, 3)` returns `[3, 3, 5, 5, 6, 7]`.
- `maxSlidingWindow(new int[]{1}, 1)` returns `[1]`.
- `maxSlidingWindow(new int[]{9, 8, 7, 6}, 2)` returns `[9, 8, 7]`.
hints: A priority queue can find each maximum, but it may leave stale values to remove.
Keep candidate indices in a deque and discard indices outside the current window.
Remove smaller values from the back before adding each new index; the front is then the maximum. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) worst-case extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: the values followed by window size, for example: [1, 3, -1, -3, 5, 3, 6, 7] 3
